{"regions":[{"label":"Figure 7.5 — Three distinct approaches to handling cross-border data flows","kind":"diagram","bbox":[0.093,0.472,0.898,0.929],"summary":"Infographic compares limited, conditional, and open transfers models by regulatory options, key features, and examples, arranged along a data-closure to data-openness spectrum.","details":"The figure is organized into three model groups, with vertical row labels at left: “Regulatory options,” “Key features,” and “Examples.” Left-to-right, from greater data closure toward greater data openness:

• Limited transfers model (blue), divided into three regulatory-option columns:
  – Domestic storage. Key feature: broad requirements to use domestic servers for data storage. Examples: China—certain personal data; US states—government data; Australia and United Kingdom—health data; Russian Federation—telecommunications data.
  – Domestic processing. Key feature: broad requirements to use domestic servers for data processing. Example: Russian Federation—processing of personal data.
  – Government approval. Key feature: prior approval required for data transfers. Example: China—Cybersecurity Law.
• Conditional transfers model (green), regulatory option “Regulatory safeguards.” Key features: consent; adequacy findings; private sector assessment (for example, codes of conduct, binding corporate rules, contractual arrangements). Example: European Union—General Data Protection Regulation.
• Open transfers model (orange), regulatory option “Private standards.” Key features: no a priori mandatory requirements; private sector accountability based on voluntary standards. Examples: US federal rules; APEC Privacy Framework.

A horizontal gradient arrow beneath the groups runs from “Data closure” on the left to “Data openness” on the right. Source: WDR 2021 team, based on Casalini and López González (2019); Cory (2017). Note: APEC = Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation.","limitations":"The graphic is a categorical comparison, not a quantitative chart; it gives no numerical scale or measured values.
